subject: astronomy
title: Stars & Constellations: Star Colours & Lives
welcome_lead: Stars are born, live and die — and their colour gives away their age and heat.
meta_desc: KS3 astronomy: star colours, sizes, life cycle basics.
final_note: Blue means hot, red means cool — and bigger stars burn faster.

concepts.def: A huge, cool, reddish star in old age.
Small, dense leftover of a dead Sun-like star.
The explosion of a giant star.
Cloud of gas and dust — where stars are born.

walkthroughs.body_html: Hotter stars look blue or white; cooler ones look yellow, orange or red. Our Sun is a friendly yellow medium star.
Stars are born in nebulae — vast clouds of gas and dust that collapse under gravity until fusion starts in the core.
Small stars become white dwarfs. Massive ones explode as a supernova and may leave a black hole or neutron star behind.
